EU/EEA.basis: Directive 2006/116/EC, Article 1(1): life plus 70 years, with the term running from 1 January following the relevant event. Pushkin died in 1837; the term ended 31 December 1907. The work was first published in 1835 during his lifetime, so the 25-year first-publication right for previously unpublished posthumous works in Article 4 is not applicable. Article 10(2) does not revive a work that was already out of copyright before 1 July 1995. If the 1977 source edition qualifies for the maximum 30-year scientific/critical edition right under Article 5, that term ended by 31 December 2007.

Germany.basis: UrhG Sections 64 and 69: 70 years after the author's death, calculated at the end of the calendar year; expiry 31 December 1907. Section 70's 25-year right for a qualifying scientific edition published in 1977 expired by 31 December 2002. Section 71's posthumous-work right does not apply because the story was first published in 1835 while Pushkin was alive.

Netherlands.basis: Official Business.gov.nl guidance: copyright expires 70 years after the creator's death, counted from 1 January of the following year. The term ended 31 December 1907. The story was published during the author's lifetime.

Poland.basis: Polish Copyright and Related Rights Act Article 36: 70 years from the author's death; Article 39 calculates full years. The term ended 31 December 1907. If the 1977 source edition qualifies as a scientific/critical edition under Article 99², its 30-year related right expired by 31 December 2007. The first-publication right under Article 99¹ does not apply because the work was already lawfully published in 1835.

Russia.basis: Civil Code Article 1281 now states life plus 70 years, but Federal Law No. 231-FZ Article 6 applies the extended term only where the previous 50-year term had not expired by 1 January 1993. For an author who died in 1837, the former 50-year term had expired by the end of 1887; the later extension does not revive it. The original work is public domain in Russia.

United States.basis: U.S. Copyright Office Circular 22 states that U.S. copyright in any work published before 1 January 1931 has expired by operation of law. This work was first published in 1835.

International screening.basis: WIPO's 2026 guide to the Berne Convention notes examples of longer national terms of 100 years after death in Mexico and 99 years in Côte d'Ivoire. Even a conservative life-plus-100-year term for an author who died in 1837 would have expired by the end of 1937. The source text is also licensed through a global CC BY-SA 4.0 transcription, and the original cover is CC0 1.0. No country-specific exception keeping the economic rights alive in 2026 was identified in the sources checked.
International screening.scope_note: Это международная кабинетная проверка по применимым основным рынкам и международным источникам, а не формальное заключение юриста по каждой стране. При добавлении конкретного рынка с особым сроком охраны требуется повторная проверка.
